$schema_note: Hand-verified game knowledge, NOT mechanically extracted from Hero_Siege.exe/data.win: these Controller_obj variable names are not present in Hero_Siege.exe (a static reading); the runtime fills the slots the code reads them through from data.win at run time, and no extractor currently produces them or ties them to Controller_obj, so they were found live, by content search. No generator produces this file or reads it; see docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md section '## 17. Stash Special Tabs & the Crafting Route' for the full write-up and ForgePact issue #14 (ForgePact/docs/crafting-materials-research.md) for the research.

materials.cell_path_note: the array being two-level is measured; the [x][y] axis order is from the static reading, not itself probed live

save.second_argument_note: as the close supplied it; its meaning is not measured

crafting_cube.note: whether the game's own count walks this grid is not observed; the grid's persistence across a save does not gate the build, per the owner's design (2026-09-24): only the craft's own items are placed here, at the press, and consumed at once

bag_to_stash_move.note: The routines the game's own Ctrl + left click runs to move one item from the bag into the stash tab on show, in that order, and the shapes that reproduced the move by name (ForgePact #68). Self and other are the two UI_Inventory_Grid_obj nodes told apart by uiNodeCallstack: InventoryGrid (the bag's, rebinding to the bag view on show) and StashGrid (the stash's, rebinding to the tab on show). The Socketable tab merges by name (socket_merge, Live 1f and 1g); placing a kind it does not hold yet was moved by hand only and has no by-name shape.

validate.arguments: the item struct; called again after the placement with self the StashGrid node
validate.answer: empty text, a refusal included (the Socketable tab's refusal of jewels shows nothing in it)

stack.arguments: the shown tab's cell array; 0 and 13 into the personal page, 9 and 2 into a shared page, the Materials tab and the Socketable tab; the item struct; the count to merge (1 on every hand move; the whole count merged by name); a small number (0 on a page and the Materials tab, 8 on the Socketable tab)
stack.answer: true after merging into a stack of the item's identity on that array; false when there is none, and then the grid placement follows

grid.arguments: the shown tab's cell array (the StashGrid node's nodeGrid on a page, Controller_obj.stashMaterialTab on the Materials tab), the item struct, 0, undefined
grid.answer: a struct of tabNumber, x, y, tabType, success; success=false when that array has no room, and no other tab is tried; tabNumber read 0 on shared page 1 too

source_clear.arguments: the item's anchor cell node in the bag grid's nodeGrid, read [y][x], then undefined; after a by-name placement (which leaves the item in its bag cells) or a merge, while the item is still on map 0 and before the owner step

socket_merge.container: the Socketable tab has no one array: one UI_Inventory_Grid_obj per item on the tab, its uiNodeCallstack StashSocketGrid, its nodeGrid one cell holding that item, whose key answers on map 9 (Controller_obj.stashSocketItemSlot is not the container); saved in stash.hss under socket_tab
socket_merge.arguments: the nodeGrid of the StashSocketGrid node holding the item's identity; 9; 2; the item struct; its count (1 measured); 8. Self and other the bag's grid node with its Socket view on show; no ValidateItem before it. Then source_clear on the bag cell, only after that node's item's o rose by exactly the count
socket_merge.answer: true, the node's o rising by the count (an orb, base id 118: 81 to 82, twice); a gem (base id 38) merged the same way and gained o=2, so no non-stackable answer was met on this tab

owner_step.arguments: 0, 9, the item's key as text; only after a placement the re-read confirmed (alone, on an item still in the bag, it leaves the key on no map)

shared.map: not established: after the owner step the key answers on neither map 0 nor map 9 by GetItemFromFingerprint, as every shared-page key does

materials.owner_step: 0 to 9 for a new identity; none for a merge

socketable.owner_step: none for a merge (by name, Live 1f and 1g); 0 to 9 for a new identity, by hand only (Live 1e)

cases: a class-10 item by hand and by name into the personal page and shared page 1, and against the full shared page 2
a new material identity by hand and by name into the Materials tab, one-unit and whole-stack (15) merges
a rune, a gem and an orb into the Socketable tab by hand; jewels and an Incarnation Gem refused by the game
an orb (base id 118) and a gem (base id 38) merged by name into their StashSocketGrid nodes on the Socketable tab, count 1

ui_node_api.note: The game's own UI node routines, as the in-game Move all button uses them (ForgePact #68). Measured in Live 1f and 1g unless an entry says R, a static reading. A node's click is its user event 15, run from the owning window's Step with self the node, other the window and one argument, the node's activationArgs, handed to its activationFunc; with activationFunc undefined the event does nothing (R; measured in Live 1g only that no armed routine logged a call with such a node as self and no dialog appeared).

sort_node.activation: gml_Script_InventorySortTab, bound with the Sort node itself as self; activationArgs [1]

create.arguments: x; y; the object index; the activation (undefined leaves activationFunc undefined); the call-stack name, stored as the node's uiNodeCallstack. Self and other the window that will own the node. Answers the node (visible 0 that frame, 1 the next)

remove.arguments: the node; self the window that owns it. The window's own close destroys a node still in its list; a tab switch keeps it

set_activation.arguments: the node; a script, bound as a method whose self is the node when callable, else activationFunc left undefined. A node bound to UiSetFloatingToFalse ended the game when clicked (that script is written for another object)
set_activation.measured: M (the dispatch and the crash); the binding rule R

move.arguments: the node; x; y. Sets both and runs the node's own position update

cases: one Materials-tab entry the bag stacks (Greater Unstable Dust, class 14, b=51)
one Socketable stack of 10 (Pristine Ruby, class 15, b=51)
